finds.quote: The war was fought over slavery. Its settlement reorganized the labor topology of an already integrated capitalism. It abolished the noun as a legal form. It put the verb under contract, pledged it as debt, brokered it across regions and oceans, and kept a penal exception through which the state could hire out the convicted body. The freedpeople's own general strike forced the opening; the settlement closed it toward contract and debt. The first fruit of the war, as Marx counted it, was a fight over the length of the day: the measure of the verb.
finds.note: Central thesis at its fullest (4.21): settlement reorganized labor topology; abstract (l.52) and §6 (l.238) restate it.

finds.quote: **4.18** The thesis this paper began from held that the North fought to free cheap wage labor for its industry. The record divides it.
finds.note: The deposit tests the founding thesis (North fought for cheap wage labor) and divides it: supported for postwar discipline/debt/brokerage/penal exception, refuted on cause, scale, supply. Quote is 4.18; the division is at 4.19 (l.194) and 4.20 (l.196).

finds.quote: **5.15** Along the axis of measurement, the unit shrinks. Life, under the life-cycle appraisal; day, under the hand rating's "expected production per day", Hammond's "hired by the day" and the eight-hour fight; task, under Taylor; motion and second, under Ford's 13 min 10 s.[^44][^67][^83][^113][^124] As the unit shrinks the legal claim narrows: capital gives up title to the lifetime and gains a finely specified claim on the contracted interval. Own less of the worker; specify more completely what working is. The worker can remain juridically indivisible while the work is divided almost without limit.
finds.note: Thesis that the unit of measurement shrinks as the juridical claim narrows.

finds.quote: **1.19** The hand is the hinge evidence of this paper. It grades a whole person's daily output as a fraction of an adult male standard: a verb-measure attached to a noun.[^44] The price (asset) and the rating (performance) met in the individual record. The plantation therefore built two abstractions at once: the person as priced asset, and the person as measured productive capacity. Rosenthal's prime-hand unit is the evidence; the inference is this paper's.
finds.note: Thesis that the plantation built two abstractions at once (priced asset and measured capacity, the 'hand'); explicitly marked as the paper's inference.

finds.quote: The span over which the noun was measured was set by the replacement market. The grain of measurement is therefore its own axis, independent of the scope of the claim: slavery could already contract its unit to the years it took to use a person up, to the day's quota and to the fraction of a hand. What emancipation changed was the scope of the claim. The grain had its own history inside slavery, and §5 follows it after the claim narrowed.
finds.note: Thesis that measurement grain is an axis independent of juridical scope and had its own history inside slavery.

finds.quote: On these texts slavery sold the person, the noun, and wage labor sold capacity for an interval, the verb. The noun owned and the verb contracted are different relations, and the difference is legal title to the person. The next step, which none of them took, is the subject of §5: the interval itself subdivided and specified, until what is purchased is a sequence of motions in a fixed time.
finds.note: Thesis that contemporaries (Hammond, Marx, Lincoln) stated the noun/verb distinction; reading of their texts.

finds.quote: Between 1859 and 1913 the record moves from the named and numbered person to the unnamed operation. The abstraction survives its object.
finds.note: Thesis on the documentary record: from the named and numbered person to the unnamed operation.

finds.quote: Individuation persists at the point of selection, so the inversion by which slavery individualizes and Fordism standardizes, this paper's own formulation, holds for the operation and fails for the hiring.
finds.note: Self-limiting thesis: the paper's own inversion (slavery individualizes, Fordism standardizes) holds for the operation, fails for hiring.

finds.quote: And the statute disclaims "the relation of Slavery or servitude", seven months before Congress passed the Thirteenth Amendment.[^92][^13] The statute itself marks slavery and servitude as the boundary its terms require it to negate.
finds.note: Reading of the 1864 Act: the statute marks slavery/servitude as the boundary its own terms require it to negate.

finds.quote: Read at the word: the Portuguese man goes through life *under* the greatest grace, and the grace is that the gods do not show themselves. The Spanish keeps the vertical and moves it — out of the preposition ("sob", under) into the adjective ("alta", high). The man is no longer beneath the grace; he passes his life in it, and the grace has acquired an altitude: the height where gods who do not appear are.
finds.window: Reis ode of 27 September 1914; Spanish translation 2025
finds.note: The deposit's own reading of what the translator's Spanish does to Reis's line (preposition to adjective); evidence is the two texts; ll.83-85 and 89 extend it to two more odes.
